paragraphs: Adtran builds broadband access equipment and software for service providers that are extending fiber across different technologies and deployment settings. Its access platforms are meant to fit several architectures, from disaggregated designs to integrated systems. The company also sells a pluggable optics module aimed at operators of data centers working under power, cooling, space and latency limits.

Deployments run from small sites carrying a few hundred subscribers up to locations serving more than 100,000. Open APIs and OSS/BSS integration connect the equipment to systems an operator already runs, while the Mosaic software suite supplies visibility from end to end. A shared operational layer correlates signals and alarms across areas that were traditionally kept apart, so a team can see how a fault affects subscriber service before tracing where it began. Fiber monitoring runs while the fiber is in service, looking for degradation before subscribers feel it.

Customer stories on the broadband access page name a rural electric cooperative bringing fiber to parts of Indiana. Another names a municipal power and light utility building a multigigabit fiber-to-the-home network. For buyers who want to talk to someone, the contact page sets out regional office details.

quote.text: Broadband networks must scale to support higher speeds and more subscribers while adapting to different deployment models and existing infrastructure.
